title: Compatible regular presentations of a map of complete local rings
statement: Let $f:(A,\mathfrak m_A)\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a local homomorphism ($f(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$) of Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for their maximal-ideal-adic topologies [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Then there exist regular local rings $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme], complete for their maximal-ideal-adic topologies, surjective local ring homomorphisms $q:R\to A$, $v:S\to B$, and a local ring homomorphism $u:R\to S$ with $vu=fq$. The map $q$ induces an isomorphism $R/\mathfrak m_R\cong A/\mathfrak m_A$. There is a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $R$ (a set of $d=\dim R$ generators of $\mathfrak m_R$) whose images $u(t_1),\ldots,u(t_d)$ extend to a regular system of parameters of $S$. In particular $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is regular local.

source.place: More on Algebra, Tag 07NN, lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings, statement and proof. Only its regularity and parameter conclusions are stated here. The residue-field isomorphism for q is given by the proof: R is a power series ring over the residue field of A in characteristic zero or over a Cohen ring with that residue field otherwise; the displayed surjection induces that field map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-power-series-presentation] to $A$ and $B$. Since the local map $f$ induces a field homomorphism $A/\mathfrak m_A\to B/\mathfrak m_B$, the two residue fields have the same characteristic. Thus obtain surjective local maps $q:R=\Lambda_A[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $v_0:S_0=\Lambda_B[[z_1,\ldots,z_e]]\twoheadrightarrow B$, with $R,S_0$ complete regular local rings and $R/\mathfrak m_R\cong A/\mathfrak m_A$. Here the coefficient rings are both fields in residue characteristic zero and both Cohen rings in residue characteristic $p>0$. Write $J=\ker(v_0)\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S_0}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings), proof, first two sentences; the presentation is Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-field-cohen-power-series-formally-smooth], the map $\mathbf Z\to R$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_R$-adic topology. The composite $fq:R\to B=S_0/J$ is continuous: $q(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$ and $f(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$. The ideal $J$ is closed in $S_0$: [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient] makes $S_0/J=B$ separated for its quotient maximal-ideal topology, so $\bigcap_m(J+\mathfrak m_{S_0}^m)=J$. Since $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S_0}$, [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] with $I=\mathfrak m_{S_0}$, $t=r=1$ gives a continuous local homomorphism $\varphi:R\to S_0$ such that $v_0\varphi=fq$. It is local because $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S_0}$ by its explicit bound $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R^{rt})\subseteq I$ with $rt=1$; alternatively the preimage of $\mathfrak m_B$ under $v_0$ is $\mathfrak m_{S_0}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN, proof, lifting sentence; Lemmas Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs) and Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous)

proof.text: Set $S=S_0[[y_1,\ldots,y_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. By grouping monomials, $S\cong\Lambda_B[[z_1,\ldots,z_e,y_1,\ldots,y_n]]$, so [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] makes it complete and regular local. Let $v:S\to B$ be the constant-$y$ map followed by $v_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables]. It is surjective and local. The continuous map $\varphi:R\to S_0$ extends to a local map $u:R\to S$ with $u|_{\Lambda_A}=\varphi|_{\Lambda_A}$ and $u(x_i)=\varphi(x_i)+y_i$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] with coefficient map $\varphi|_{\Lambda_A}$, ideal $I=\mathfrak m_S$, and variables $\varphi(x_i)+y_i\in\mathfrak m_S$. This map is local: in the field case the $x_i$ generate $\mathfrak m_R$, and in the Cohen case its additional generator $p$ maps to $p\in\mathfrak m_S$. The composites $vu$ and $fq$ agree on coefficients and on all $x_i$ and are continuous into the complete local ring $B$; uniqueness in the evaluation lemma proves $vu=fq$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN, proof, final paragraph defining phi-prime and S-prime; completeness and regularity of the power series ring are Algebra, Remark Tag 032C

proof.text: The elements $a_i=\varphi(x_i)$ belong to $\mathfrak m_{S_0}$ since $\varphi$ is local. Substitution $y_i\mapsto a_i+y_i$, fixing $S_0$, is a continuous automorphism of $S_0[[y_1,\ldots,y_n]]$: its inverse substitutes $y_i\mapsto y_i-a_i$, and both substitutions exist by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] with coefficient ring $S_0$, target $S$ and ideal $\mathfrak m_S$. Their composites fix $S_0$ and each $y_i$, hence are the identity by uniqueness in that lemma; the substitutions preserve $\mathfrak m_S$ and are therefore continuous for its adic topology. The standard regular parameters of $S$ are $z_1,\ldots,z_e,y_1,\ldots,y_n$ in residue characteristic zero and $p,z_1,\ldots,z_e,y_1,\ldots,y_n$ in residue characteristic $p$ [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete]. Applying the automorphism gives a regular system containing $u(x_1)=a_1+y_1,\ldots,u(x_n)=a_n+y_n$. In the Cohen case it also contains $u(p)=p$, since every unital ring map fixes the integer $p$. Thus the images under $u$ of the standard regular parameters of $R$ (Step 1) form part of a regular system of parameters of $S$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN, proof, last sentence; the omitted parameter check is the displayed substitution and its inverse

proof.text: The images of the parameters of $R$ are a regular sequence in $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], applied to the regular system of $S$ from Step 4 and reordered to put those images first. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular] applies to the local map $u:R\to S$ and proves it flat.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NN, 'In particular' sentence; Algebra, Lemmas Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM) and Tag 07DY (lemma-flat-over-regular)

proof.text: The regular system of parameters in Step 4 can be reordered with $u(t_1),\ldots,u(t_d)$ first. Its first $d$ elements generate $\mathfrak m_RS$, since $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ generate $\mathfrak m_R$. By the quotient assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $S/(u(t_1),\ldots,u(t_d))=S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is regular local. This also covers $d=0$, when the quotient is $S$.
